text:
Ryan: Heads-up — product wants to roll out a change to the reranker response shape. They want per-candidate provenance + a compact scoring envelope so the Console can show cost estimates. Need engineering input on feasibility and migration plan.

Jess: Can you paste the proposed envelope?

Ryan: Sure, current naive idea from PM:```json
{
  "scores": [{"id": "c1", "score": 0.72}],
  "format": "v2-json",
  "meta": {"model": "open-rank-xl", "quant": "q4_1"}
}
```But they'd like an alternate compact mode that puts scores in a flat array and a schema version to reduce payload.

Leila: Flat arrays are fine for bytes, but we need to keep explicit candidate ids for telemetry correlation. We could do a compact mode like:```json
{"fmt": "v2c", "ids": ["c1","c2"], "s": [0.72,0.12], "m": {"mv": "open-rank-xl:2"}}
```where fmt signals compact. That would save ~40% for large candidate lists.

Omar: Two concerns: 1) quota accounting (are we charging per candidate or per request?) and 2) routing fallback rules when a model is offline. Current Dedicated billing uses "score-units" = candidates * weight(model). We must ensure compact format doesn't break cost estimation.

Jess: For billing we charge per-candidate rescore by default. If a request sets "top_k" we bill for min(n_candidates, top_k). We should document that in the API contract. Compact format is purely transport — server should expand internally and tag telemetry the same way.

Maria: UX ask: Console wants to show estimated cost before doing a rollout. They need an API to estimate cost given candidate count and model. Could expose /estimate?payload or add headers with an estimated unit count in responses.

Leila: We already compute an internal token/candidate matrix for batching heuristics. Expose a light-weight estimator endpoint is doable. But it must reflect runtime routing: e.g., if a route policy might send 20% to fallback cheaper model, estimator should apply routing policy to estimate. Otherwise Console numbers will be wrong.

Ryan: Good point. Proposal: estimator must accept a routing_profile param that matches the Console rollout config. Example:```
POST /v1/rerank/estimate
{ "candidates": 150, "routing_profile": "canary-20-open-rank-xl" }
```returns {"units":1234, "breakdown": [{"model":"open-rank-xl","pct":80,"units":987},{"model":"open-rank-s","pct":20,"units":247}], "assumptions": "no prefix cache" }

Jess: Telemetry: add fields on request and response spans: score_format (v2-json|v2c), model_variant, candidate_count, routed_model, kv_cache_hit_rate, scoring_ms. That will let dashboards show regressions when we flip formats or models.

Omar: About deprecation: we currently support legacy "scores" envelope (v1). We should not break it. Plan: support both v1 and v2-json for 6 months, v2c (compact) opt-in behind a header X-Rank-Format: v2c. After stable rollout and metrics, then notify deprecation with 90-day window.

Maria: UX flow: in Console rollout UI show a toggle for response format (v1|v2-json|compact) with a tooltip: "Compact reduces payload; may make debugging harder." Also show per-candidate estimated cost and a sample response preview.

Leila: Implementation notes: runtime will accept fmt header and do early-path parsing for v2c (fast path). We must add a small parser for ids+s arrays and ensure consistent mapping to internal per-candidate objects (id, score, provenance). Also add a flag to telemetry to record whether compact was used.

Jess: Quotas: add an enforcement check on total candidates after any expansion (i.e. after upstream candidate generation). We should fail fast with 413-like error: code RERANK_TOO_MANY_CANDIDATES and include allowed_max in the response. Also add a soft limit metric to warn console.

Ryan: Decision draft: - Accept v2-json and v2c as new formats; v1 supported during migration. - Compact (v2c) behind opt-in header for 3 months, then allow Console to flip to opt-out for enterprise. - Add /estimate endpoint and telemetry tags. - Enforce per-request candidate hard limit of 1000 (configurable per customer). - Add console preview and per-candidate cost display.

Omar: One more: routing fallback rules. If preferred model is unavailable, fallback should be to the next model in affinity list. Telemetry should tag routed_model and fallback_reason. For SLA we will expose route_policy id in response meta.

Maria: I'll file a Console PR for the rollout UI and estimator integration. Patch notes and in-console banner for affected customers.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: rerank-format-parser branch -> staging at 2028-07-14T21:30:00Z (CI green).

Jess: I'll follow up with a short API changelog draft and a migration guide (examples for client SDKs). Anyone object to the above plan?

Leila: No objections. +1 on the opt-in phase.

Omar: +1. I'll start adding telemetry keys and estimator stub.

Ryan: Great — I'll coordinate the deprecation timeline with support and PM. Thanks everyone.
